subject: Temporary in-flight transfer commitments & subprocessor timeline — MedZen DPA follow-up
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medzenhealth.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medzenhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question: in-flight transfers, pin window, and subprocessor notice

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our legal review for MedZen's pilot, our DPO asked for two clarifications before we proceed to signature:

1) In-flight transfers: can Redwood commit that customer data (tokenized model inputs) will not be routed outside the EU/US/APAC region mid-request except under documented, timebound contingency windows? If so, what is the maximum allowed "in-flight" window (hours) and what triggers it?

2) Subprocessor timeline: if Redwood needs to activate a new subprocessor (e.g., edge cache or analytics), what notice period will MedZen receive, and can we get a short-run roster for Q2 (who already has access)?

We want to avoid a broad "may transfer" line in the DPA and prefer concrete operational limits. Attached is our standard DPA redline for reference.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Data Protection, MedZen Health
Attachment: MedZen_DPA_v3.pdf (redline)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Quick question: in-flight transfers, pin window, and subprocessor notice

Team — forwarding MedZen's note. TL;DR: they want concrete commitments around (a) in-flight processing that crosses regions mid-request and (b) a short notice / roster for subprocessor activations.

Questions for legal/product:
- Product: what operational windows do we practically support today for in-flight cross-region routing (e.g., failover <48h for cache sync, ephemeral crosshop during instance spin-up)? Can we translate into hours/minutes and define triggers (region outage, capacity failover, security incident)?
- Legal: suggested DPA text or addendum that maps to those operational windows without overcommitting. Can we offer a bounded contingency: e.g., transient cross-region hop up to X hours only for incident remediation and logged with customer notification within Y hours?

I attached a working draft playbook (inflight-transfer-playbook-draft.docx) with proposed operational language. Please reply with redline suggestions — I need to get a single reply back to Elena by EOD tomorrow so they can finish procurement.

Thanks — karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: inflight-transfer-playbook-draft.docx

From: mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick question: in-flight transfers, pin window, and subprocessor notice

Karthik / Aditya —

Thanks for the draft. I reviewed the playbook and pushed a few changes. Summary of proposed legal-friendly commitments we can offer without escalating to CS or infra changes: 

1) In-flight transfer (operational carveout):
- Commitment: "Redwood will ensure that customer request processing is routed to the customer-selected region (US / EU / APAC) by default. In the event of a region-specific outage or capacity emergency, transient cross-region processing (a single in-flight hop) may occur solely to complete in-progress requests or to failover to capacity; such transient processing will be limited to a maximum of 72 hours per incident and will be logged and reported to the customer within 24 hours of the event's start."
- Rationale: 72 hours is a defensible upper bound that aligns with our existing capacity failover and cache sync timelines. We should be clear that this is incident-only, not routine.

2) Subprocessor activation notice and roster: 
- Commitment: "Redwood will provide at least 14 days' notice before activating any new subprocessor with access to customer data in production; in emergency cases (security/ops incident) Redwood will notify the customer within 48 hours and provide a post-event report."
- Roster: attached csv is the Q2 roster of subprocessors with a short purpose field. (See subprocessor_roster_2027Q2.csv)

3) Auditability: include a clause that logs of any transient cross-region hops (timestamp, origin/destination region, triggering event, affected request IDs) will be made available to the customer on request as part of incident reporting.

Open items for product before we send to MedZen:
- Confirm the 72-hour upper bound is technically feasible for cache sync / failover scenarios (Aditya).
- Confirm we can deliver logs with the granularity above within our incident reporting timeline (Laura).

If both say yes, I'll craft a short DPA addendum paragraph and we can propose it to Elena.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
Attachments: subprocessor_roster_2027Q2.csv

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medzenhealth.com>, MedZen Legal <legal@medzenhealth.com>
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question: in-flight transfers, pin window, and subprocessor notice

Elena / Raj —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short version: we can offer a bounded operational commitment and a notice/roster cadence. Below is the proposed customer-facing language we would be comfortable putting in an addendum to the DPA; legal and infra have reviewed it and flagged no blockers pending the items listed. If this is acceptable to MedZen we can add it as an annex.

Proposed addendum language (summary):
- Default routing: requests are routed to the customer-selected region (US / EU / APAC).
- Transient in-flight processing: in the event of a region outage, capacity emergency, or security incident, Redwood may perform a single transient cross-region hop to complete in-progress requests or to fail over; such transient processing will be limited to 72 hours per incident and will be logged. Redwood will notify the customer within 24 hours of the event start and provide detailed logs and a post-incident report on request.
- Subprocessor activation: Redwood will provide no less than 14 days' prior notice for new subprocessors that will have access to production customer data. For emergency activations, Redwood will notify the customer within 48 hours and provide a post-event report.
- Auditability: logs related to any transient cross-region processing (timestamps, origin/destination regions, triggering event, request IDs) will be available upon request for incident review and regulatory purposes.

Attachments: we included the current Q2 subprocessor roster and a one-page operational playbook for how transient hops are initiated and logged.

Next steps: if this language looks good, I'll ask Mina to prepare a one‑paragraph DPA addendum and we can circulate for signature. If you need tighter windows (e.g., 24 hours instead of 72), let us know — that'll be a product/ops conversation and we can map the trade-offs.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
